_comment: The world map: holdings (DESIGN §5). Terrain and site placement are derived from a stable map seed, so the save stores only what the player has done. Every number here is a first-pass default and flagged _tuning unless DESIGN states it.
_tuning: Overnight 2026-09-28, Claude's first pass on everything DESIGN §5 does not fix: site weights, yields, tier costs and times, the treasure, the watchtower's reach, the troop field's men. For Mathias to tune.

sites.name: Forest
sites.description: Standing oak within a day’s haul.

sites.name: Clay bank
sites.description: A cut bank of good throwing clay.

sites.name: Farmland
sites.description: Flat ground the river floods and feeds.

sites.name: Quarry
sites.description: Good building stone. Nothing to cut it for until stone is worked (DESIGN §4.1).

sites.name: Salt spring
sites.description: Brine that dries white. Idle until salt is traded (DESIGN §4.1).

sites.name: Troop field
sites.description: Veterans and their sons, settled on land in return for service. Adds to the militia without drawing on the colony’s own people.

sites.name: Watchtower
sites.description: A high place with a long view. Holding it shows the country around it, and a raid against anything in sight is seen a round sooner.

sites.name: Ford
sites.description: A crossing the traders use. While it is held, trade at the forum comes cheaper.

sites.name: Shrine
sites.description: A grove the tribes hold sacred. A small standing gravitas to the house that keeps it.

sites.name: Ruin
sites.description: Older than Rome, and someone wrote things down. A prize, not an income: the scrolls come once, when it is first held.

sites.name: Buried hoard
sites.description: Coin in a rotted chest. The scouts bring it home and there is nothing left to hold.

sites.name: Barbarian camp
sites.description: Warriors, and they saw your scout first.

_sites: DESIGN §5.2 ✅ kinds. Ids kept from v0.1 where the kind already existed (timber = Forest, meadow = Farmland, ruins = Ruin). A shrine's gravitas goes to the player's house until a temple post exists (✅ Mathias, 2026-09-28). Quarry and salt spring are claimable and idle until their content drop (🟡 per §5.2). A ford's effect is a trade bonus at the forum; envoys already arrive in one round (Mathias, 2026-09-28).

scout._comment: Prepared like an envoy (DESIGN §3.2): dispatched now, resolves at the next round.

hold._comment: Exposure rises with distance (DESIGN §5.3). A garrison is the only thing that answers it.

tiers._comment: DESIGN §5.3 ✅: camp, station, fort, built in place on the village clock, one holding under construction at a time beside the building and the field. Yield and defence rise with the tier; the numbers are _tuning.

contest._comment: DESIGN §5.5, the contest rule, which follows from §2.11. An unclaimed site may be taken by a tribe at any time, the player away or not: a missed opportunity, permitted. A held site changes hands only in a round the player convenes: a tribe's move against it is declared in one round and decided in a later one, after the player's own move, so the militia can be sent first.
contest._tuning: Claude's first pass, 2026-09-28: the hourly chance a tribe takes one unclaimed site (0.02, about three a week), the share of the map's sites tribes may hold (0.3), and the rounds between a move being declared and decided (1; a held watchtower in sight adds one).

roads._comment: DESIGN §5.4: roads built segment by segment, hex to hex, from the colonia outward, one segment under construction at a time (Mathias, 2026-09-28). A holding joined to the colonia by an unbroken road: raid exposure falls, yield rises, and trade moves more easily. v0 roads cost denarii and wood; a paved upgrade with stone waits for the stone drop.
roads._tuning: Claude's first pass, 2026-09-28: a segment's cost (30 denarii, 40 wood) and time (15 minutes); a connected holding's raid chance halved (exposureCut 0.5) and its yield raised by a quarter (yieldBonus 0.25); the trade rate sharpened by 0.1 while any holding is connected.
